## `BUILD.md`

````markdown
# Building CleanForge

> This project was patched in an environment with **no Android SDK, no Gradle, no Kotlin compiler and no network**, so none of the commands below have been run against it yet. Treat the first build as the real test, and read "If the first build fails" below. A successful CI run from a clean checkout (with the Gradle wrapper committed) is the proof the audit asks for; nothing else is.

## Prerequisites

- JDK 17
- Android SDK with platform **35** and build-tools (Android Studio installs these)
- Gradle 8.9 (only to generate the wrapper once), or just open the project in Android Studio (Ladybug or newer)

## One-time: generate and COMMIT the Gradle wrapper

`gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` is in the repository, but the wrapper **jar and scripts are not** (they are binaries that could not be produced where this project was patched). The independent audit requires them to be committed, because a repository that cannot be built with `./gradlew` from a clean checkout cannot be verified.

```bash
gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.9      # needs Gradle 8.9 installed once; Android Studio does the same on import
git add gradlew gradlew.bat gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
git commit -m "Add Gradle wrapper"
```

No Gradle locally? Push to GitHub: the CI job generates a temporary wrapper, builds everything, uploads it as the `gradle-wrapper` artifact, and then **fails on purpose** until you commit those files. Optionally pin the Gradle download with `distributionSha256Sum` in `gradle-wrapper.properties` (value from <https://gradle.org/release-checksums/>), and keep `gradle/actions/wrapper-validation` in CI, which checks the committed jar against Gradle's official releases.

Point `local.properties` at your SDK if needed: `sdk.dir=/path/to/Android/Sdk`.

## Commands

```bash
./gradlew clean :app:testDebugUnitTest   # 91 unit tests (JVM, Linux/macOS)
./gradlew :app:lintDebug                 # report: app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.html
./gradlew :app:lintDebug -PstrictLint    # same, but lint errors FAIL the build (CI uses this)
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug       # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease     # app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk (or app-release.apk if signed)
```

Rename outputs to `CleanForge-debug.apk` / `CleanForge-release.apk` if you like; the build uses Gradle's default names.

Unit tests use the JDK "unix" file-attribute view, so run them on Linux/macOS/WSL (or in the included CI).

## Signing a release build

```bash
keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore cleanforge-release.jks -alias cleanforge \
        -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000
```

Create `keystore.properties` in the project root (git-ignored):

```
storeFile=cleanforge-release.jks
storePassword=...
keyAlias=cleanforge
keyPassword=...
```

Without it, `assembleRelease` produces an **unsigned** APK that Android will not install. Keep the keystore safe: losing it means you can never ship an update.

Verify a signed APK: `apksigner verify --print-certs app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`

## Install on the phone

```bash
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```

Then grant All-files access (and Shizuku permission if you use it). See `README.md`.

## No SDK locally? Use CI

`.github/workflows/build.yml` compiles, tests, lints (strict, non-blocking until the first clean baseline: then delete `continue-on-error`) and builds both APKs on GitHub's runners and uploads them (plus reports) as artifacts. Push the project to a GitHub repository and open the *Actions* tab. It runs the exact commands above through `./gradlew`.

## If the first build fails

Library versions were chosen without registry access (AGP 8.7.2, Kotlin 2.0.21, KSP 2.0.21-1.0.27, Hilt 2.56, Compose BOM 2024.11.00, Shizuku 13.1.5). If Gradle cannot resolve one, bump it in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` (keep KSP's prefix equal to the Kotlin version).

The places most likely to need a small adjustment because they touch APIs I could not check against a compiler:

1. `core/shizuku/ShizukuFileServiceConnector.kt`: `Shizuku.UserServiceArgs` builder methods, `bindUserService` / `unbindUserService(args, connection, remove)` signatures.
2. `core/shizuku/ShizukuManager.kt`: Shizuku listener signatures, `getVersion()`, `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale()`.
2a. `aidl/.../IFileService.aidl`: the `in String[]` argument and the appended methods 6 to 12 must generate cleanly.
2b. `core/shizuku/AidlPrivilegedFileApi.kt`: `DeadObjectException`, `TransactionTooLargeException`, `RemoteException` handling.
3. `di/AppModule.kt` and the `@HiltViewModel`: Hilt/KSP generation errors are verbose; fix the first one listed.
4. `ui/*`: Material 3 parameter names if you bump the Compose BOM.
5. `app/src/main/aidl/.../IFileService.aidl`: explicit transaction ids (`= 16777114`) need AGP's AIDL support enabled (`buildFeatures.aidl = true`, already set).

After it compiles, run the tests; a failing test is information about a real behaviour, not noise, because every test encodes a safety rule from `SECURITY.md`.

## Verifying on the phone (recommended before real use)

1. Create a throwaway folder in Download with some files and run a Review scan; confirm the dialog lists exactly what you ticked.
2. With Shizuku running, scan, and confirm that cache and leftover findings appear and that deleting one clears only that app's cache contents.
3. Try to break it: tick a photo in DCIM, then edit or replace the file before confirming; the report should say it was skipped.

## Shizuku engine tests (Part 2)

`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` runs, among others, `FileServiceCoreTest`, `WireCodecTest`, `PrivilegedExecutorTest`,
`CapabilityRegistryTest`, `MaintenanceModelTest`, `ScanRepositoryTest`, the extended `CleaningEngineTest`,
`ScannerEvidenceTest` and `PolicyGuardTest`. They run the real service logic over a fake filesystem and a fake service.
`PrivilegedExecutorTest` and `CapabilityRegistryTest` use real time on purpose (deadlines of 150 to 750 ms). They do **not**
cover Binder, the AIDL stub, `ShizukuFileServiceConnector`, `ShizukuManager` or `AidlPrivilegedFileApi`; those need the
device checklist in `docs/SHIZUKU_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md` (section 8).
````

## `CHANGELOG.md`

```markdown
# Changelog

All notable changes to CleanForge. Format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/).

---

## [1.0.0] — Part 5: UI/UX Polish & CI/CD

### Added
- GitHub Actions CI pipeline: unit tests, lint, debug + release APK builds
- Gradle wrapper binary committed and validated in CI
- Material 3 dynamic color on Android 12+, static scheme on Android 11
- RAM gauge integrated into Home screen as an expandable card
- `LazyColumn` keys changed from path-only to category+path (fixes crash on duplicate paths)
- Final Compose UI polish: animations, transitions, empty states

### Changed
- `PolicyGuardTest`: lint gate now hard-fails on `abortOnError` with `-PstrictLint`
- NavHost: RAM screen accessible via Home card tap or direct nav route

### Fixed
- Gradle wrapper missing binary (CI now generates and validates it)
- Review screen crash when a path is flagged by two scanners simultaneously

---

## [0.5.0] — Part 4: RAM Monitoring

### Added
- `core/memory/RamSnapshot.kt` — honest memory reading with `MemoryPressure` levels
- `core/memory/MemInfoParser.kt` — pure `/proc/meminfo` parser (no I/O, fully testable)
- `core/memory/MemoryInfoProvider.kt` — `ProcMemInfoProvider` reads `/proc/meminfo`
- `core/memory/ClearMemoryResult.kt` — measured freed bytes, never estimated
- `domain/usecase/ObserveRamUseCase.kt` — periodic `Flow<RamSnapshot>`
- `domain/usecase/ClearMemoryUseCase.kt` — honest `killBackgroundProcesses` with measured delta
- `ui/RamViewModel.kt` — StateFlow-based UI state, start/stop observation
- `ui/screens/RamScreen.kt` — circular gauge, pressure colors, honest explainer
- `KILL_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` permission (documented, deliberate, not creep)
- `MemInfoParserTest.kt` — 8 tests covering parsing, fallbacks, pressure, corruption
- `ClearMemoryUseCaseTest.kt` — 4 tests covering honest measurement, UNKNOWN state, exceptions

### Changed
- `PolicyGuardTest.kt`: permission assertion updated from 2 → 3 permissions
- `di/AppModule.kt`: added `ActivityManager` and `MemoryInfoProvider` bindings

### Design Decisions
- No "boost" claims. UI explicitly states Android manages RAM intentionally.
- `freedBytes` is measured from `MemAvailable` delta, clamped to ≥ 0.
- Packages in `InstallState.UNKNOWN` are never killed (fail-closed).

---

## [0.4.0] — Part 3: Storage Forensics

### Added
- `CleaningCategory.FORENSIC_MEDIA` — app-specific media & caches, `isQuick = false`
- `core/scanner/WhatsAppScanner.kt` — `.Statuses` (>24h), `Sent` folders, old DB backups (>7d)
- `core/scanner/TelegramScanner.kt` — Video/Audio/Images/Documents cache (>14d)
- `core/scanner/TikTokScanner.kt` — video + `.music` cache (>7d)
- `core/scanner/TwitterXScanner.kt` — media cache (>7d)
- `core/scanner/InstagramScanner.kt` — media cache (>14d)
- `SafetyValidator.isKnownForensicPath()` — strict allowlist for forensic paths
- `ProtectedApps.MESSAGING` set — messaging apps never pre-selected
- `docs/FORENSICS_MATRIX.md` — full forensic scanner documentation

### Changed
- `SafetyValidator.kt`: `FORENSIC_MEDIA` allowed in `Android/media` and `Android/data` via allowlist
- `SafetyValidator.kt`: personal folder protection extended to block forensic rules
- `ScanItem.kt`: `reasonForFlagging` field for evidence-based UI display
- `Enums.kt`: `FORENSIC_MEDIA` category added

### Security
- Forensic paths are allowlisted per-package, per-subfolder. No wildcard `Android/data` access.
- All forensic items: `isPreselected = false`, `requiresShizuku = true`, `DeleteMode.FILE`
- WhatsApp/Telegram/Instagram in `ProtectedApps.MESSAGING` — extra caution layer

---

## [0.3.0] — Part 2: Shizuku Engine

### Added
- `core/shizuku/ShizukuFileServiceConnector.kt` — bind/unbind/death/reconnect lifecycle
- `core/shizuku/ShizukuFileService.kt` — AIDL user-service implementation
- `core/shizuku/AidlPrivilegedFileApi.kt` — typed adapter over raw AIDL
- `core/privileged/FileServiceCore.kt` — privileged-side file operations
- `core/privileged/WireCodec.kt` — serialization for binder transport
- `core/privileged/PrivilegedExecutor.kt` — centralized execution, accepts `MaintenanceRequest` not raw paths
- `core/backend/ShizukuFileBackend.kt` — read-only Shizuku backend (no delete)
- `core/backend/Capabilities.kt` — runtime capability detection
- `core/backend/PackageInventory.kt` — tri-state `installState()` (INSTALLED / NOT_INSTALLED / UNKNOWN)
- `core/shizuku/ShizukuManager.kt` — Shizuku lifecycle state holder
- `app/src/main/aidl/com/cleanforge/shizuku/IFileService.aidl` — versioned AIDL contract
- `docs/SHIZUKU_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md` — operation support matrix
- 25 new Shizuku-specific tests

### Changed
- `CacheScanner`: uses Shizuku backend for `Android/data/<pkg>/cache`
- `CorpseScanner`: uses Shizuku backend for `Android/data` and `Android/obb` leftovers
- `CleaningEngine`: re-validates Shizuku availability before every privileged deletion
- `CleanViewModel`: Shizuku state exposed via `StateFlow`, actionable error states in UI
- `PolicyGuardTest`: 4 new guards for privileged surface (no shell, no generic delete, AIDL versioning, no direct Shizuku API in UI)

### Security
- Shizuku service runs as user-service, NOT root
- AIDL contract uses fixed transaction IDs (only grows, never reassigns)
- `setProtectedPackages` prevents privileged deletion of messaging app data
- Service death → operation halts → auto-rebind → user informed

---

## [0.2.1] — Security Re-Audit

### Fixed
- H1: `MATCH_UNINSTALLED_PACKAGES` no longer used as proof of "installed"
- M1: Confirmation dialog shows full evidence for every item
- M2: Duplicate keeper chosen by user, not by age
- M3: Child-level TOCTOU narrowed (lstat re-check before every remove)
- M4: Multi-user wording corrected (current user/profile only)

---

## [0.2.0] — Part 1: Audit & Refactor

### Added
- Complete project restructure to standard Gradle layout
- `SafeDeleter` — bounded, symlink-safe, mount-aware deletion
- `SafetyValidator` — lexical + policy gate for every deletion
- `PlanBuilder` — refusal tracking with human-readable reasons
- `CleaningEngine` — revalidation at execution time
- 9 evidence-based scanners
- Material 3 UI with 3-tab navigation
- 66 JUnit tests across 6 suites
- `PROJECT_AUDIT.md`, `BUILD.md`, `SECURITY.md`

### Removed
- Hidden API usage (`IPackageManager`, `IPackageDataObserver`, `AppGlobals`)
- Untrusted Maven repository (`api.xposed.info`)
- Unused dependencies (Room, WorkManager, DataStore)
- Broken navigation references to non-existent screens

### Fixed
- 10 build blockers (B1–B10)
- 9 safety/data-loss findings (S1–S9)

- AI-generated project scaffold (pre-audit)
- 35 source files, 2 test classes
- Multiple critical issues (see PROJECT_AUDIT.md)
```

## `PART_B_AUDIT.md`

```markdown
# CleanForge Part B audit: privileged layer (Shizuku)

Scope: `core/privileged/*` (10 files), `core/shizuku/*` (6 files), `AndroidManifest.xml`, `proguard-rules.pro`, and the five Part B tests (`CapabilityRegistryTest`, `FileServiceCoreTest`, `MaintenanceModelTest`, `PrivilegedExecutorTest`, `WireCodecTest`). Part B sources were byte-identical to the copies in the Part A zip; none had been read before this audit.

## Bugs found and fixed

| # | Severity | File | Bug | Fix |
|---|----------|------|-----|-----|
| 1 | High | `privileged/FileServiceCore.kt` | `list()` built `ListReply(..., detail = ...)`, but `ListReply` has no `detail` parameter: the module did not compile. | Removed the argument. `FileServiceCoreTest` already expects `OS_DENIED` with no names. |
| 2 | Low | `shizuku/ShizukuFileServiceConnector.kt` | `acquire()` and `restart()` made Shizuku status and bind/unbind binder calls on the caller's thread (possibly main), contradicting the `PrivilegedSessionProvider` contract. | Both now run on `Dispatchers.IO`. |
| 3 | Low | `shizuku/ShizukuManager.kt` | Shizuku's listeners fire on the main thread and `refresh()` makes binder calls (also from `register()` in `Application.onCreate`), against its own "never on main" note. | Listeners and `register()` refresh on a worker; `refresh()` is `@Synchronized` so an older reading cannot overwrite a newer one. |
| 4 | High (cross-part) | `fs/SafeDeleter.kt` (Part A) | Compared `st_dev` of every ancestor from `/storage`, which is a tmpfs on Android. Every real deletion through this service (and the app) came back `REFUSED`. | Only folders below `/storage/emulated/0` are inspected, as non-symlink directories; no device comparison. Regression tests added. |

## Checked and found sound

- **Service core:** only two delete shapes (`Android/data|obb/<pkg>` tree, `Android/data/<pkg>/cache` contents); installed-apps guard required for tree deletes; own package never deletable; identity (dev/ino) required; ancestors and symlinks checked.
- **Protocol:** `WireCodec` bounds match the service caps (20k names, 255-char names); transaction ids match the AIDL contract test.
- **Executor and registry:** write lock plus read permits, deadlines with restart, post-delete verification, and capability states all behave as the tests describe. No lock cycle between registry, executor and connector.
- **Manifest:** permissions match `PolicyGuardTest` (exactly `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, `KILL_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES`); `ShizukuProvider` correctly declared; `allowBackup=false`; no INTERNET.
- **ProGuard:** the user-service constructor, `IFileService$Stub` and the AIDL interface are kept.

## Remaining items, now resolved

- **Unreachable forensic cleanup (Android/data):** by design. `TikTokScanner`, `TwitterXScanner` and `InstagramScanner` are dormant (not registered) because the service has no single-file delete. They are now documented as dormant in their KDoc. Registering them requires a new, strictly allowlisted file-delete shape first.
- **Per-item revalidation cost:** `CleaningEngine` now asks for the full package list and the Shizuku capability probe once per run (per-package install state and Shizuku authorization are still asked per item).
- **Platform scanners did not compile** (`isPreselected` constructor argument, old nullable backend API): WhatsApp, Telegram, TikTok, Twitter and Instagram scanners are now thin subclasses of `ForensicFolderScanner`, matching `ForensicScannersTest`.

## Tests

- Not compiled or run: the sandbox has no Kotlin/Gradle toolchain and `testutil/Fixtures.kt` was not supplied. All changes were checked by reading code against tests, plus brace and paren balance.
- Regression tests added for the cross-part fixes: `SafeDeleterTest` (3), `StorageWalkerTest` (4, new), `PlanBuilderTest` (2), `CleaningEngineTest` (2), `ForensicValidatorTest` (1), `ScanRepositoryTest` (1), `StandardFileBackendTest` (1, new).
- Run: `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`.

## Still needed from you

- **Part D:** confirm `buildFeatures { buildConfig = true }` (the Shizuku files use `BuildConfig.DEBUG`, `APPLICATION_ID`, `VERSION_CODE`).
- **`di/AppModule.kt`:** `CleaningEngine` has no `@Inject`; it must be provided there, and the executor and registry must be singletons (each owns a coroutine scope).
- **`testutil/Fixtures.kt` and `IFileService.aidl`:** to compile the tests and verify the stub signatures.
```

```markdown
# CleanForge Part C audit: scanners and RAM

Scope: `scanner/*` (Apk, Cache, Corpse, Duplicate, EmptyDirectory, LargeFile, Log, Temp, Thumbnail, plus the five platform scanners and `ForensicFolderScanner`), `memory/*` (5 files), `ClearMemoryUseCase`, `ObserveRamUseCase`. The Part C zip was byte-identical to the original files already in hand. The platform scanners and `ForensicFolderScanner` were audited earlier; this pass read the rest.

## Bugs found and fixed

| # | Severity | Where | Bug | Fix |
|---|----------|-------|-----|-----|
| 1 | High | `WhatsApp/Telegram/TikTok/TwitterX/InstagramScanner` | Did not compile: passed `isPreselected` to the `ScanItem` constructor (it is derived) and used the old nullable backend API; they also swallowed cancellation through `runCatching`. | Rewritten as thin subclasses of `ForensicFolderScanner` (rules and thresholds kept, matching `ForensicScannersTest`). TikTok/Twitter/Instagram documented as dormant (no single-file delete in the Shizuku service). |
| 2 | Medium | Apk, LargeFile, Duplicate, EmptyDirectory, Log, Temp | A walk cut off at the entry limit, or entries that could not be read, were never reported, so "could not check" looked like "nothing found" (violates `Scanner.incompleteReasons`). | New `WalkNotes`/`walkNoting` collects truncation and unreadable entries; all six scanners now report them. Unreadable log heads and un-listable folders are counted instead of skipped silently. |
| 3 | Medium | `ThumbnailScanner` | "Only small files, no sub-folders" was claimed even if part of the folder was cut off or unreadable; a missing-vs-denied folder looked the same; no cancellation check. | Fails closed (an unknown part means "not a cache"), reports why, distinguishes missing from denied, checks cancellation. |
| 4 | Low | `MemInfoParser` | `MemTotal: 0` produced a zero-byte snapshot instead of "unknown". | Returns null. |
| 5 | Low (compile hazard) | `BackgroundProcessKiller` | `catch (_: Exception)` is not valid on older Kotlin versions. | Named the parameter. |
| 6 | Low | `ApkScanner` | Parsing each APK (slow) had no cancellation check. | Added. |

## Checked and found sound

- `CacheScanner` / `CorpseScanner`: installed vs known stay separate, tri-state install state, plausibility floor, exact folder type, age, lower-bound sizes.
- `DuplicateScanner`: staged hashing, hard links excluded, never picks a keeper.
- `LargeFileScanner`: bounded heap, never pre-selected. `EmptyDirectoryScanner` and `TempScanner` rules match their docs.
- Memory: `/proc/meminfo` parsing, pressure bands, measured (not estimated) freed bytes, system apps and CleanForge itself are never trimmed.

## Notes (not changed)

- `ClearMemoryResult.processesTouched` counts kill REQUESTS sent, not processes that existed; Android does not let us see others' processes. Word the UI as "asked N apps to trim".
- `ClearMemoryUseCase` calls `isCurrentlyInstalled` once per known package (hundreds of binder calls); acceptable, but a single installed-apps query would be faster.

## Tests

- Not compiled or run (no Kotlin/Gradle here, `testutil/Fixtures.kt` missing). Checked by reading code against tests and brace/paren balance.
- Added: `WalkScannerReasonsTest` (4, new), `MemInfoParserTest` (+1). Run `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`.
```

## `README.md`

```markdown
# CleanForge

A free, open-source, offline-first storage cleaner for Android 11+.
Made by **Aman**.

No ads. No subscription. No telemetry, analytics or accounts.
No internet permission. No root.

---
[![Download APK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-Android_APK-2ea44f?logo=android&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lightibulb/CleanForge/releases/download/v2.5.4/CleanForge-debug.apk)

## Features

### 🔍 Evidence-Based Cleaning
Every item CleanForge flags carries **proof** of why it's safe to delete.
Filename or extension alone is never accepted as evidence.

| Scanner | What it finds | Evidence required |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|
| App Caches | `Android/data/<pkg>/cache` contents | Package installed + exact path match |
| Leftovers | Folders of uninstalled apps | Package unknown to OS + age ≥ 14 days |
| Thumbnails | `DCIM/.thumbnails` | Only small files, no sub-folders |
| Incomplete Downloads | `.crdownload`, `.part`, `.partial` | Age ≥ 7 days + Download folder only |
| Log Files | `*.log` in Downloads | Text content verified + age ≥ 30 days |
| Large Files | Files over threshold | Top-N by size, never pre-selected |
| Duplicates | Same content, different paths | Staged hashing, user picks what goes |
| APK Installers | `.apk` files | Platform parser reads manifest |
| Empty Folders | Verifiably empty directories | `rmdir` semantics only |

### 🔬 Storage Forensics (Part 3)
Deep, app-specific scanning for known cache and media patterns.
All forensic items are **never pre-selected** — the user always decides.

| App | What's scanned | Safety rule |
|-----|---------------|-------------|
| WhatsApp / WhatsApp Business | `.Statuses` (>24h), `Sent` folders, old DB backups (>7d) | Shizuku required, FILE mode only |
| Telegram | Video/Audio/Images/Documents cache (>14d) | Shizuku required, FILE mode only |
| TikTok / TikTok Lite | Video cache, `.music` cache (>7d) | Shizuku required, FILE mode only |
| Twitter/X / X Lite | Media cache (>7d) | Shizuku required, FILE mode only |
| Instagram / Instagram Lite | Media cache (>14d) | Shizuku required, FILE mode only |

### 📱 Shizuku Integration (Part 2)
On Android 11+, `Android/data` and `Android/obb` are invisible to normal apps.
CleanForge uses [Shizuku](https://shizuku.rikka.app/) as a **user-service** (not root) to:

- **Read** `Android/data/` and `Android/obb/` for scanning
- **Clear** app caches (`CONTENTS_ONLY` on exact `cache/` path)
- **Remove** leftovers of uninstalled apps (`TREE` on exact package folder)

Without Shizuku, those scanners are skipped with a visible notice.
CleanForge **never** claims Shizuku grants root or unrestricted access.

### 🧠 RAM Monitoring (Part 4)
Honest, transparent memory information. No fake "boost" claims.

- Reads `/proc/meminfo` (no permission needed)
- Shows total, used, available, and cached memory
- Color-coded pressure indicator (LOW → CRITICAL)
- Optional "Clear background apps" action using `KILL_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES`
  - Measures the **actual** freed bytes, never estimates
  - Tells you the truth: Android may reload apps, using more battery

### 🛡️ Safety Model
- **Fingerprint verification**: Every file is `lstat`-ed at scan time and re-checked before deletion
- **Symlink protection**: Never follows symlinks; symlink roots are refused
- **Mount boundaries**: Never crosses filesystem boundaries
- **Depth/entry limits**: Bounded walks prevent runaway recursion
- **No shell**: Zero `Runtime.exec`, `ProcessBuilder`, or `sh -c` anywhere
- **No `deleteRecursively`**: All deletion goes through `SafeDeleter`
- **Personal data zones**: DCIM, Pictures, Movies, Music, Documents, Download, WhatsApp, Telegram — only individually reviewed files, never pre-selected
- **Messaging apps protected**: WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Messenger, etc. are never pre-selected

---

## Architecture

Enforced by types: scanners emit evidence-bearing `ScanItem`s, `PlanBuilder` yields a
`CleaningPlan` with refusals and reasons, `confirmedByUser()` is the only path to a
`ConfirmedPlan`, and `CleaningEngine` accepts nothing else.

| Layer | Package | Responsibility |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| Filesystem | `core.fs` | `FsOps`, `SafeDeleter`, `PathRules`, `StorageWalker` |
| Safety | `core.safety` | `SafetyValidator` — lexical + policy gate |
| Scanners | `core.scanner` | 9 base + 5 forensic scanners |
| Cleaning | `core.cleaning` | `PlanBuilder`, `CleaningEngine` |
| Backend | `core.backend` | `FileOperationBackend`, `PackageInventory`, `Capabilities` |
| Shizuku | `core.shizuku` | `ShizukuFileServiceConnector`, AIDL adapters |
| Privileged | `core.privileged` | `FileServiceCore`, `WireCodec`, `PrivilegedExecutor` |
| Memory | `core.memory` | `RamSnapshot`, `MemInfoParser`, `MemoryInfoProvider` |
| Domain | `domain.usecase` | `ScanDevice`, `ExecuteCleaningPlan`, `ObserveRam`, `ClearMemory` |
| DI | `di` | Hilt modules |
| UI | `ui` | Compose screens, ViewModels, Material 3 |

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full diagram and
[ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md](ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md) for the forward-looking proposal (not yet built).

---

## Permissions

| Permission | Why |
|-----------|-----|
| `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` | Read/delete user-selected files in shared storage |
| `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES` | Know which apps are installed (never guess from folder names) |
| `KILL_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` | Honest RAM clear (Part 4). Only trims reclaimable processes |

**No `INTERNET`. No `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`. No analytics. No ads. Ever.**
Enforced by `PolicyGuardTest`.

---

## Requirements

- Android 11 (API 30) or later
- [Shizuku](https://shizuku.rikka.app/) (optional — needed for `Android/data` / `Android/obb`)
- `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` granted in Settings → Special access

## Build

See [BUILD.md](BUILD.md).

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## License

CleanForge is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the **GNU General Public License v3.0 or later** as published by the Free Software Foundation.

This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but **WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY**; without even the implied warranty of **MERCHANTABILITY** or **FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE**. See the [GNU General Public License](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html) for more details.

*Created and owned by **Aman**.*

---

## Credits

- **Created & owned by**: Aman
- **Shizuku**: [RikkaApps](https://github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku)
```

## `SECURITY.md`

```markdown
# Security and safety model

CleanForge deletes files. The design goal is that it can never delete something you did not see, understand and confirm.

## Pipeline (no step may be skipped)

`SCAN -> CLASSIFY -> VALIDATE -> PLAN -> USER CONFIRMATION -> REVALIDATE -> DELETE -> VERIFY -> REPORT`

| Step | Where | What it guarantees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SCAN / CLASSIFY | `core/scanner/*` | A finding is a *proposal with evidence*, never a command. |
| VALIDATE / PLAN | `SafetyValidator`, `PlanBuilder` | Path policy, mode policy, overlap rules, and the duplicate rule: the copy that stays is one the user did NOT tick; a group whose every copy is ticked is refused. Refused items are *kept with their reason*. |
| USER CONFIRMATION | `ConfirmDialog` | Lists EVERY item with its full path, why it was flagged, confidence, risk, exactly what is deleted, *"no undo"*, Shizuku need, and for duplicates KEEP / DELETE CANDIDATE; refusals too. `CleaningEngine` accepts only a `ConfirmedPlan`. |
| REVALIDATE | `CleaningEngine.processItem` | Policy again, live permissions, fresh package-state check (app cache: package *currently installed*; leftover: package not known and not installed), scan-time fingerprint, kept-copy check. |
| DELETE | `SafeDeleter` (app or Shizuku service) | No symlink following, no mount crossing, bounded depth/entries, directory identity re-checked, and every entry re-`lstat`ed and identity-compared immediately before it is removed. |
| VERIFY / REPORT | `CleaningEngine`, `ReportDialog` | Re-stat after deletion; freed bytes come from what was really removed. |

## Hard rules enforced in code

- Only the canonical root `/storage/emulated/0` is accepted. Aliases (`/sdcard`, `/storage/self/primary`) are refused.
- Paths with `..`, `.`, empty segments, trailing slash, NUL/control characters, or over 4096 chars are refused.
- Structural names are compared case-insensitively (the filesystem is case-insensitive).
- Recursive deletion only for: `Android/data/<pkg>/cache` (contents), `Android/{data,obb}/<pkg>` (uninstalled app, TREE), `DCIM/.thumbnails` (contents).
- `Android/data`, `Android/obb`, `Android/media` and every top-level storage folder can never be deleted.
- Inside DCIM, Pictures, Movies, Music, Documents, Download, Recordings, Audiobooks, Podcasts, Ringtones, Alarms, Notifications, WhatsApp, Telegram: single files only, only after you tick them, never pre-selected.
- Pre-selection is limited to well-evidenced app caches of non-messaging apps. Large, old, duplicate, or unknown never means junk.
- No shell is ever started and no command line is built from a file name. A test fails the build if `Runtime.exec`, `ProcessBuilder` or `Shizuku.newProcess` appear.
- The Shizuku service trusts nothing from the app process: it re-checks each path and allows only the two recursive shapes above. All of its logic is in `FileServiceCore`, which also refuses any path whose ancestors below the storage root are not real directories (a symlink in the middle of a path is not followed), refuses a tree delete for any package in the installed-apps guard (any letter case) or for CleanForge itself, and refuses every tree delete until the app has pushed that guard.
- The app never sends a path to be deleted. It sends a typed request (clear the cache of package P / remove the leftover of package P); the executor validates the package identifier and builds the path itself. Package identifiers containing `/`, `..`, spaces, control characters or shell metacharacters have no target.
- Failures are never read as success or as absence: a failed read is `Unavailable`/`Denied`/`Failed`, not "not found" and not "empty"; a failed package-manager query is `UNKNOWN`, not "not installed".
- Fail closed: if the package list cannot be read or looks implausibly small (`MIN_PLAUSIBLE_PACKAGES` is only a fail-closed guard, not proof the query worked), leftover and cache findings are not produced and deletion is skipped.
- Two different package questions. `knownPackageNames()` = "Android still has an identity for this name" (includes apps uninstalled with their data kept); `isCurrentlyInstalled()` = "installed right now". An app cache is only ever offered, and only ever deleted, for a package that is currently installed. A data-kept uninstalled package is neither an app cache nor a leftover: it is left alone. Both checks cover the current Android user/profile only; other users and work profiles are not enumerated.
- Duplicates. CleanForge never decides which copy you want (age proves nothing). Every copy is listed, none is pre-ticked, you tick what to delete, one copy you did not tick is pinned as the keeper (and re-checked, unchanged, right before deleting), and it can never plan the deletion of every copy, also not via another list such as large files.

## Storage Forensics (Part 3)

Forensic scanners target known app-specific cache/media patterns. They are strictly narrower than a general walk:

- Category `FORENSIC_MEDIA`, `isQuick = false` (on-demand only), `requiresShizuku = true`, `isPreselected = false`, `DeleteMode.FILE` only.
- Paths are matched against a **per-package, per-subfolder allowlist** in `SafetyValidator.isKnownForensicPath()`. No wildcard `Android/data` or `Android/media` access.
- Allowed shapes include `Android/media/<pkg>/WhatsApp/Media/.Statuses/*`, `.../Sent/*`, `.../Databases/msgstore-*`, `Android/media/<pkg>/Telegram/Telegram {Video,Audio,Images,Documents}/*`, and `Android/data/<pkg>/cache/*` for TikTok / Twitter-X / Instagram.
- Messaging apps (WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Signal, Messenger, etc. in `ProtectedApps.MESSAGING`) are never pre-selected and get an extra caution layer.
- Forensic rules never apply inside personal folders; the personal-zone protection blocks them.

## RAM Monitoring (Part 4)

- Memory info is read from `/proc/meminfo` (world-readable, no permission needed). Nothing is estimated or faked; if the file can't be read the UI shows "unknown", never zero.
- The optional "Clear background apps" action uses `ActivityManager.killBackgroundProcesses` and requires the `KILL_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` permission.
- Freed bytes are **measured** from the `MemAvailable` delta before/after and clamped to ≥ 0. If memory did not actually increase, the app reports 0 freed — it never invents a number.
- Packages whose install state is `UNKNOWN` (failed query) are never killed (fail-closed).
- The UI states plainly that Android manages RAM intentionally and that clearing is temporary and may use more battery. CleanForge makes **no "boost" or speed claim**.

## Privacy

- No INTERNET permission, no analytics, ads, telemetry or accounts, no cloud processing. Enforced by `PolicyGuardTest`.
- Permissions: `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` (list and delete what you select), `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES` (know which apps are installed for the current user/profile), and `KILL_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` (honest RAM clear, Part 4).
- `allowBackup=false`.

## Shizuku

Shizuku is not root. By default its user service runs as the shell user and it executes no commands: the service has a fixed set of file operations and no shell. If you start it in root mode, CleanForge shows that and applies exactly the same path rules. It is optional: without it, only the Android/data cleaners are disabled.

## Known residual risks

- **Race between last check and removal.** Android exposes no `unlinkat`/`openat` to Kotlin, so a process with write access to the same folder could swap an entry between our last `lstat` and `remove`. Mitigations: identity (type, device, inode) of each folder is re-checked before its entries are removed, and of every single entry again immediately before its own `remove` (a swapped entry is left untouched and reported), `remove` never recurses, and symlinks are unlinked as links only, so a swap can never make deletion follow a link. The two calls are still separate, so the window is narrowed, not closed. Shared storage does not allow apps to create symlinks, which makes this hard to exploit. Covered by `SafeDeleterTest`.
- **Inode reuse.** Inode numbers can be reused by the filesystem after a delete, so an identity check cannot detect a replacement that happens to receive the same inode. File fingerprints therefore also compare size and modification time.
- **Leftover folders can hold game saves.** They are marked "Check first", never pre-selected, never reversible.
- The installed-apps guard in the service protects against a logic bug in the app, not against a hostile caller (only the app Shizuku authorized can reach the service at all).
- A cancel request that arrives before a delete has started in the service is not remembered; the app-side wait ends at once, but a delete already dispatched may still finish. The result is then reported as confirmed or unconfirmed from what is observed afterwards.
- **RAM clear is limited.** `killBackgroundProcesses` only trims processes Android already considers reclaimable; it cannot free memory held by foreground or persistent apps, and Android may reload the apps afterwards.
- Not yet verified on a real Vivo device or Funtouch OS. Behaviour of Android/data through Shizuku on Android 11 follows the documented model but must be confirmed on hardware.
- This code has not been compiled or run in the environment where it was audited and patched, and the Gradle wrapper jar is not in the repository. See `BUILD.md`. Treat every statement in this file as a design claim until CI has run the tests.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report privately to the maintainer, Aman. Add a contact address or issue-tracker link here before publishing: `<contact: TODO by Aman>`.
```

```markdown
# CleanForge update 2: features and fixes

Built on your uploaded repo (the CI build that works). Not compiled or run here; the CI build is the test.

## Backend
| Request | What changed |
|---|---|
| Scan shows nothing | Results now appear **as each batch arrives** (before, nothing showed until a whole scanner finished, which on a slow Shizuku scan looks empty). After a scan a **"What the scan checked"** card lists every scanner and what it found ("App caches: 38 found (412 MB)", "Thumbnails: nothing found"); skipped or failed scanners still get their amber note with the reason. Tell me what that card says if it is still empty. |
| Memory: which app eats RAM | New read-only call in the Shizuku service (`processMemoryEx`, app processes only, no argument) + `TopProcessesUseCase`. The Memory hero is tappable; a list slides down from behind it and refreshes every 4 s while open. Needs Shizuku; without it the card says why. `versionCode` bumped to 4 so Shizuku restarts the service with the new call. |
| Storage card by type | New `StorageBreakdownUseCase`: Images, Videos, Audio, Documents (from Android's media index, by top folder), Apps you installed (installed code, top apps) and Caches and junk (from your last scan), plus "System and other". Tap the storage hero; tap a category for its sub-categories. |
| Run scan "useless" | Same fix as the first row, plus the hero ring no longer stays empty (it only animated from its first, still-zero value). |

Limits that Android sets, not the app: private app data is hidden from other apps (so the Apps row is installed code), and per-app memory is resident memory including pages shared with the system.

## UI
- **Theme follows the system** by default. About has a Theme button cycling System, Light, Dark.
- **Review: "Select everything & delete…"** ticks every suggestion (keeps one copy per duplicate group), then opens the normal confirmation listing every path. Nothing is removed without that confirmation.
- **Nav bar** is now opaque, higher contrast, with a border and shadow.
- **Easter egg sheet**: it sat halfway up because a Compose dialog window wraps its content and is centred; the window now fills the screen and anchors the sheet to the bottom.
- **Animations**: tab changes slide and fade by direction, cards expand and collapse with springs, rows animate selection and size, the rings follow live values.

## Housekeeping
- `apply-update2.sh` deletes the three stray copies in `app/src/test/java/com/cleanforge/data/` (Preferences, ScanModels, Verses).
- Tests added: `ProcessMemoryTest`, `ThemeModeTest`, and a summaries test in `ScanRepositoryTest`.

## Remaining
- Send me the CI result (or the first error) after this update, and what the new scan card says on your phone.
- App Android/data and obb sizes per app (needs a new Shizuku call, like memory); not included.
```

## `app/src/main/aidl/com/cleanforge/shizuku/IFileService.aidl`

```
package com.cleanforge.shizuku;

/**
 * Runs inside the Shizuku "user service" process (shell UID 2000, or root if the user
 * started Shizuku in root mode). It is the ONLY place privileged filesystem work happens.
 *
 * Every method re-validates its arguments; the app process is not trusted blindly.
 * Nothing here ever spawns a shell or builds a command line from a path.
 *
 * COMPATIBILITY RULE: ids 1-5 and destroy() never change meaning. New methods are only appended with new ids.
 * Ids 2-5 are the original null-means-everything methods; the app no longer calls them (it uses the *Ex methods,
 * which say WHY there is no value) but the service still answers them for an older app build.
 * Reply layouts of the *Ex methods are defined and unit-tested in WireCodec.kt; bump PrivilegedProtocol.API_VERSION
 * when one changes.
 */
interface IFileService {
    // Transaction id reserved by Shizuku for service teardown.
    void destroy() = 16777114;

    int uid() = 1;

    /** [type, size, mtimeMs, dev, ino] or null if missing / not allowed. Never follows symlinks. */
    long[] lstat(String path) = 2;

    /** Child NAMES (not paths) of an allowed directory, or null. Capped in size. */
    String[] list(String path) = 3;

    /** [bytes, complete(0/1)] or null. Bounded walk; never crosses mounts or follows symlinks. */
    long[] directorySize(String path) = 4;

    /** [status, entriesRemoved, bytesFreed]. Directory identity (dev, ino) is mandatory. */
    long[] delete(String path, int mode, long dev, long ino, boolean hasIdentity) = 5;

    // ---- appended in protocol version 1 ----

    /** Protocol version of the running service (PrivilegedProtocol.API_VERSION). */
    int apiVersion() = 6;

    /** [status] or [status, type, size, mtimeMs, dev, ino]. Status values: see ReplyStatus. */
    long[] statEx(String path) = 7;

    /** ["<status>", "<truncated 0/1>", name...]. Total name length is bounded to stay below the binder limit. */
    String[] listEx(String path) = 8;

    /** [status] or [status, bytes, complete(0/1), unreadableDirs]. Bounded walk. */
    long[] sizeEx(String path) = 9;

    /** ["<status>", "<entriesRemoved>", "<bytesFreed>", "<detail>"]. Status values: see DeleteStatus. */
    String[] deleteEx(String path, int mode, long dev, long ino, boolean hasIdentity) = 10;

    /** Stops the delete in progress before its next entry. Best effort; a delete not yet started is unaffected. */
    void cancelCurrent() = 11;

    /** Replaces the installed-apps guard for tree deletions. Returns names accepted, or -1 if the list was rejected. */
    int setProtectedPackages(in String[] packages) = 12;

    /**
     * Read-only: one line per running APP process (uid >= 10000), "pid|uid|rssKb|processName". Takes no argument, so
     * there is nothing for the caller to point at. Used for the "what is using memory" list.
     */
    String[] processMemoryEx() = 13;
}
```

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge

import com.cleanforge.data.ThemeMode
import androidx.compose.foundation.isSystemInDarkTheme
import android.graphics.Color
import android.os.Bundle
import androidx.activity.ComponentActivity
import androidx.activity.SystemBarStyle
import androidx.activity.compose.setContent
import androidx.activity.enableEdgeToEdge
import androidx.compose.runtime.DisposableEffect
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.lifecycle.compose.collectAsStateWithLifecycle
import com.cleanforge.data.Preferences
import com.cleanforge.ui.CleanForgeApp
import com.cleanforge.ui.theme.CleanForgeTheme
import dagger.hilt.android.AndroidEntryPoint

/** @AndroidEntryPoint is required: the app gets its ViewModels from Hilt. */
@AndroidEntryPoint
class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        enableEdgeToEdge()
        setContent {
            val context = LocalContext.current
            val prefs = remember { Preferences(context) }
            val mode by prefs.themeMode.collectAsStateWithLifecycle(initialValue = ThemeMode.System)
            val dark = when (mode) {
                ThemeMode.System -> isSystemInDarkTheme()
                ThemeMode.Light -> false
                ThemeMode.Dark -> true
            }

            // Bar icons must contrast with the theme the user chose in About (they were fixed to "light").
            DisposableEffect(dark) {
                enableEdgeToEdge(
                    statusBarStyle = SystemBarStyle.auto(Color.TRANSPARENT, Color.TRANSPARENT) { dark },
                    navigationBarStyle = SystemBarStyle.auto(Color.TRANSPARENT, Color.TRANSPARENT) { dark }
                )
                onDispose { }
            }

            CleanForgeTheme(dark = dark) {
                CleanForgeApp(prefs = prefs)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## `app/src/main/java/com/cleanforge/core/backend/Capabilities.kt`

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.backend

import android.os.Environment
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.CapabilityRegistry
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.CapabilityStatus
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.OperationCapability
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.PrivilegedOperation
import com.cleanforge.core.shizuku.ShizukuManager
import com.cleanforge.core.shizuku.ShizukuState

/** Live answers (never cached) to "what am I allowed to do right now?". */
interface Capabilities {
    fun hasAllFilesAccess(): Boolean

    /** Shizuku is running and CleanForge may use it. Says nothing about any particular operation. */
    fun shizukuAuthorized(): Boolean

    /**
     * Fresh answer for one privileged operation, with an actionable reason. The default only knows whether Shizuku is
     * authorized; the real implementation runs a read-only probe through the capability registry.
     */
    suspend fun readiness(op: PrivilegedOperation): OperationCapability =
        if (shizukuAuthorized()) {
            OperationCapability(op, CapabilityStatus.PREREQUISITES_MET, "Shizuku is authorized")
        } else {
            OperationCapability(op, CapabilityStatus.UNAVAILABLE, "Shizuku is not available right now")
        }
}

class AndroidCapabilities(
    private val shizuku: ShizukuManager,
    private val registry: CapabilityRegistry
) : Capabilities {
    override fun hasAllFilesAccess(): Boolean = Environment.isExternalStorageManager()

    override fun shizukuAuthorized(): Boolean {
        shizuku.refresh() // permission can be revoked at any time; never trust a stale value
        return shizuku.state.value is ShizukuState.Authorized
    }

    override suspend fun readiness(op: PrivilegedOperation): OperationCapability = registry.probe().of(op)
}
```

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.backend

import com.cleanforge.core.fs.DeleteMode
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.DeleteResult
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsStat
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.SizeResult

/** Child names of a directory. [truncated] means the listing was cut at a safety bound: there are more entries. */
data class DirListing(val names: List<String>, val truncated: Boolean = false)

/**
 * The read side of a backend. Every call says WHY it has no value ([FsResult]); none of the failure cases may be
 * treated as "nothing there".
 */
interface FileReadBackend {
    val name: String

    suspend fun lstat(path: String): FsResult<FsStat>
    suspend fun list(path: String): FsResult<DirListing>

    /** [SizeResult.isExact] is false when a safety bound cut the walk short or sub-folders were unreadable. */
    suspend fun directorySize(path: String): FsResult<SizeResult>
}

/**
 * Where ordinary (non-privileged) filesystem work happens: this app's own process. Privileged work does NOT go
 * through this interface; it goes through [com.cleanforge.core.privileged.PrivilegedExecutor].
 */
interface FileOperationBackend : FileReadBackend {
    suspend fun delete(path: String, mode: DeleteMode, expected: FsStat?): DeleteResult
}
```

## `app/src/main/java/com/cleanforge/core/backend/FsResult.kt`

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.backend

/**
 * Outcome of a READ at the backend boundary. Replaces the old "null means everything" convention, where
 * `null` could mean missing, refused, empty, or "the Shizuku service is dead", and callers could not tell which.
 *
 * Callers must decide per case; none of the failure cases may ever be treated as "nothing found" or "already gone".
 */
sealed interface FsResult<out T> {
    /** The operation ran and produced [value]. */
    data class Ok<out T>(val value: T) : FsResult<T>

    /** The path was looked up successfully and does not exist. This is an answer, not a failure. */
    data object NotFound : FsResult<Nothing>

    /** The path policy or the OS refused the request. The data may exist; we were not allowed to see it. */
    data class Denied(val why: String) : FsResult<Nothing>

    /** The channel itself was not usable: no Shizuku, no permission, bind timeout, service died, call timed out. */
    data class Unavailable(val why: String) : FsResult<Nothing>

    /** The operation ran but could not complete (I/O error, unexpected reply). */
    data class Failed(val why: String) : FsResult<Nothing>
}

/** The value if the call succeeded, otherwise null. Use ONLY where every failure case may safely be ignored. */
fun <T> FsResult<T>.valueOrNull(): T? = (this as? FsResult.Ok<T>)?.value

/** True for every outcome in which we do NOT know whether the path exists (anything except Ok and NotFound). */
val FsResult<*>.isInconclusive: Boolean
    get() = this is FsResult.Denied || this is FsResult.Unavailable || this is FsResult.Failed

/** Human-readable reason for an inconclusive result, or null for Ok/NotFound. */
fun FsResult<*>.reasonOrNull(): String? = when (this) {
    is FsResult.Denied -> why
    is FsResult.Unavailable -> why
    is FsResult.Failed -> why
    else -> null
}
```

## `app/src/main/java/com/cleanforge/core/backend/PackageInventory.kt`

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.backend

import android.content.Context
import android.content.pm.ApplicationInfo
import android.content.pm.PackageManager

/**
 * Fail-closed guard, NOT proof that a package query succeeded. A real device always has far more than this
 * many packages, so a smaller list almost certainly means the query failed or was filtered, and callers then
 * produce no findings and skip deletions. An explicit failure is reported as `null` by
 * [PackageInventory.knownPackageNames]; this count is only a second line of defence on top of that.
 */
const val MIN_PLAUSIBLE_PACKAGES = 20

data class ArchiveInfo(val packageName: String, val versionCode: Long)

/**
 * What Android says about ONE package name for the current user/profile. A folder under Android/data is never evidence
 * for any of these: the answer comes only from the package manager.
 */
enum class InstallState {
    /** Installed right now. */
    INSTALLED,

    /** Uninstalled but Android kept its data: it has an identity, but it is not installed. */
    UNINSTALLED_DATA_KEPT,

    /** The package manager has no record of this name for this user (authoritative "not found"). */
    NOT_KNOWN,

    /** The query failed for any other reason. NOT the same as "not installed": callers must fail closed. */
    UNKNOWN
}

/**
 * What the OS knows about apps, for the CURRENT Android user/profile only (other users and work profiles are
 * not enumerated). Never inferred from folder names.
 *
 * Two different questions, two different methods. Never use one where the other is meant:
 *  - [knownPackageNames]: does Android still have an identity for this name (installed OR uninstalled with data kept)?
 *  - [isCurrentlyInstalled]: is the app installed right now?
 */
interface PackageInventory {
    /**
     * Every package the OS still knows about for the current user/profile, INCLUDING ones uninstalled with
     * their data kept. It is NOT evidence that an app is installed. Its job is to stop data-kept packages from
     * being called "leftovers". Null when the query failed (callers must then do nothing, never assume
     * "nothing is installed").
     */
    fun knownPackageNames(): Set<String>?

    /**
     * True only if [packageName] is installed for the current user/profile right now. A package that is merely
     * known (uninstalled with data kept) is NOT installed. Fails closed: any error answers false.
     */
    fun isCurrentlyInstalled(packageName: String): Boolean

    /**
     * The authoritative per-package answer. Which way to fail closed depends on the caller (a cache is only cleared
     * for INSTALLED, a leftover is only removed for NOT_KNOWN), so a failed query is [InstallState.UNKNOWN] and never
     * silently becomes "not installed".
     *
     * The default derives the answer from the two methods above and is meant for fakes; [AndroidPackageInventory]
     * overrides it with a single package-manager lookup.
     */
    fun installState(packageName: String): InstallState {
        val known = knownPackageNames() ?: return InstallState.UNKNOWN
        return when {
            isCurrentlyInstalled(packageName) -> InstallState.INSTALLED
            packageName in known -> InstallState.UNINSTALLED_DATA_KEPT
            else -> InstallState.NOT_KNOWN
        }
    }

    fun installedVersionCode(packageName: String): Long?

    /** Reads an APK with the platform parser. Null if it is not a readable APK. */
    fun archiveInfo(apkPath: String): ArchiveInfo?
}

class AndroidPackageInventory(context: Context) : PackageInventory {
    private val pm: PackageManager = context.applicationContext.packageManager

    @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
    override fun knownPackageNames(): Set<String>? = try {
        pm.getInstalledPackages(PackageManager.MATCH_UNINSTALLED_PACKAGES)
            .map { it.packageName }
            .toSet()
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        null
    }

    /**
     * Deliberately WITHOUT MATCH_UNINSTALLED_PACKAGES: without that flag the platform does not return packages
     * that were uninstalled with their data kept. As a second, independent check the application's
     * FLAG_INSTALLED bit must also be set (it is cleared for data-kept packages).
     */
    @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
    override fun isCurrentlyInstalled(packageName: String): Boolean = try {
        val info = pm.getPackageInfo(packageName, 0)
        val app: ApplicationInfo? = info.applicationInfo
        info.packageName == packageName && app != null && (app.flags and ApplicationInfo.FLAG_INSTALLED) != 0
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        false
    }

    @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
    override fun installedVersionCode(packageName: String): Long? = try {
        pm.getPackageInfo(packageName, 0).longVersionCode
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        null
    }

    /**
     * One lookup WITH MATCH_UNINSTALLED_PACKAGES: found + FLAG_INSTALLED = installed, found without it = uninstalled
     * with data kept. NameNotFoundException is the platform's authoritative "no such package for this user"; every
     * other failure (remote errors while system_server restarts, security errors) is UNKNOWN, not "not installed".
     */
    @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
    override fun installState(packageName: String): InstallState = try {
        val info = pm.getPackageInfo(packageName, PackageManager.MATCH_UNINSTALLED_PACKAGES)
        val app: ApplicationInfo? = info.applicationInfo
        when {
            info.packageName != packageName || app == null -> InstallState.UNKNOWN
            (app.flags and ApplicationInfo.FLAG_INSTALLED) != 0 -> InstallState.INSTALLED
            else -> InstallState.UNINSTALLED_DATA_KEPT
        }
    } catch (e: PackageManager.NameNotFoundException) {
        InstallState.NOT_KNOWN
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        InstallState.UNKNOWN
    }

    @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
    override fun archiveInfo(apkPath: String): ArchiveInfo? = try {
        pm.getPackageArchiveInfo(apkPath, 0)?.let { ArchiveInfo(it.packageName, it.longVersionCode) }
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        null
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.backend

import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsStat
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.SizeResult
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.PrivilegedExecutor

/**
 * READ access to Android/data and Android/obb through the privileged executor. Needed ONLY there on Android 11+.
 * Deliberately has no delete: privileged deletions are described as maintenance requests and run by
 * [PrivilegedExecutor.execute], never by a path-and-mode call that could aim at anything.
 * If Shizuku is unavailable every call says so ([FsResult.Unavailable]); it never falls back to guessing or a shell.
 */
class ShizukuFileBackend(private val executor: PrivilegedExecutor) : FileReadBackend {
    override val name: String = "Shizuku service"

    override suspend fun lstat(path: String): FsResult<FsStat> = executor.stat(path)
    override suspend fun list(path: String): FsResult<DirListing> = executor.list(path)
    override suspend fun directorySize(path: String): FsResult<SizeResult> = executor.measure(path)
}
```

## `app/src/main/java/com/cleanforge/core/backend/StandardFileBackend.kt`

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.backend

import com.cleanforge.core.fs.DeleteMode
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.DeleteResult
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsOps
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsProbe
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsStat
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsType
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.SafeDeleter
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.SizeResult
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.StorageWalker
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.currentCoroutineContext
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

/** Runs in the app process. Reaches shared storage with All-files access; NOT Android/data or Android/obb. */
class StandardFileBackend(private val fs: FsOps) : FileOperationBackend {
    override val name: String = "App (All-files access)"

    private val walker = StorageWalker(fs)

    override suspend fun lstat(path: String): FsResult<FsStat> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        when (val p = fs.probe(path)) {
            is FsProbe.Found -> FsResult.Ok(p.stat)
            FsProbe.Missing -> FsResult.NotFound
            FsProbe.Denied -> FsResult.Denied("The system refused access")
            FsProbe.Error -> FsResult.Failed("Could not examine the path")
        }
    }

    override suspend fun list(path: String): FsResult<DirListing> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        when (val p = fs.probe(path)) {
            is FsProbe.Found -> {
                if (p.stat.type != FsType.DIRECTORY) {
                    FsResult.Failed("Not a folder")
                } else {
                    val names = fs.list(path)
                    if (names == null) FsResult.Denied("The system refused to list this folder") else FsResult.Ok(DirListing(names))
                }
            }
            FsProbe.Missing -> FsResult.NotFound
            FsProbe.Denied -> FsResult.Denied("The system refused access")
            FsProbe.Error -> FsResult.Failed("Could not examine the path")
        }
    }

    override suspend fun directorySize(path: String): FsResult<SizeResult> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        when (val p = fs.probe(path)) {
            is FsProbe.Found -> {
                val size = walker.sizeOf(path)
                if (size == null) FsResult.Failed("Not a file or folder") else FsResult.Ok(size)
            }
            FsProbe.Missing -> FsResult.NotFound
            FsProbe.Denied -> FsResult.Denied("The system refused access")
            FsProbe.Error -> FsResult.Failed("Could not examine the path")
        }
    }

    override suspend fun delete(path: String, mode: DeleteMode, expected: FsStat?): DeleteResult =
        withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            // Cancelling the caller stops a big folder between entries instead of after the whole thing.
            val job = currentCoroutineContext()[Job]
            SafeDeleter(fs, isCancelled = { job?.isActive == false }).delete(path, mode, expected)
        }
}
```

## `app/src/main/java/com/cleanforge/core/benchmark/BenchmarkEngine.kt`

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.benchmark

import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsOps
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.FsType
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.StorageWalker
import com.cleanforge.core.fs.WalkLimits
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.currentCoroutineContext
import kotlinx.coroutines.ensureActive
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import java.io.File
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong

data class BenchmarkSample(val timestampMs: Long, val rssBytes: Long)
data class BenchmarkAccuracy(val expectedEntries: Long?, val actualEntries: Long, val match: Boolean)

data class BenchmarkReport(
    val startedAt: Long,
    val durationMs: Long,
    val entriesVisited: Long,
    val bytesSeen: Long,
    val peakRssBytes: Long,
    val samples: List<BenchmarkSample>,
    val accuracy: BenchmarkAccuracy,
    val truncated: Boolean
) {
    val entriesPerSecond: Long get() = if (durationMs > 0) entriesVisited * 1000L / durationMs else 0L
}

class BenchmarkEngine(private val fs: FsOps) {
    suspend fun run(
        root: String,
        limits: WalkLimits = WalkLimits(maxDepth = 32, maxEntries = 200_000),
        expectedEntries: Long? = null,
        sampleEveryMs: Long = 250L
    ): BenchmarkReport = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        val startedAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
        var entries = 0L
        var bytes = 0L
        var truncated = false
        var unreadable = 0
        val sampler = RssSampler(sampleEveryMs).also { it.start() }
        try {
            for (e in StorageWalker(fs).walk(
                root, limits,
                onTruncated = { truncated = true },
                onUnreadable = { unreadable++ }
            )) {
                entries++
                if (e.stat.type == FsType.FILE) bytes += e.stat.size
                if (entries % 512L == 0L) currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()
            }
        } finally {
            sampler.stop()
        }
        BenchmarkReport(
            startedAt = startedAt,
            durationMs = System.currentTimeMillis() - startedAt,
            entriesVisited = entries,
            bytesSeen = bytes,
            peakRssBytes = sampler.peak(),
            samples = sampler.samples(),
            accuracy = BenchmarkAccuracy(expectedEntries, entries, expectedEntries == null || entries == expectedEntries),
            truncated = truncated || unreadable > 0
        )
    }

    private class RssSampler(private val everyMs: Long) {
        private val _samples = ArrayList<BenchmarkSample>()
        private val peak = AtomicLong(0)
        @Volatile private var running = false
        private var thread: Thread? = null

        fun start() {
            running = true
            thread = Thread {
                while (running) {
                    val ts = System.currentTimeMillis()
                    val rss = rssBytes()
                    synchronized(_samples) { _samples += BenchmarkSample(ts, rss) }
                    peak.updateAndGet { maxOf(it, rss) }
                    try { Thread.sleep(everyMs) } catch (e: InterruptedException) { break }
                }
            }.also { it.isDaemon = true; it.start() }
        }

        fun stop() { running = false; thread?.interrupt(); thread?.join(500) }
        fun peak(): Long = peak.get()
        fun samples(): List<BenchmarkSample> = synchronized(_samples) { _samples.toList() }

        /** Android: real RSS from /proc/self/statm. JVM: 0. Never throws. */
        private fun rssBytes(): Long {
            val android = runCatching {
                val f = File("/proc/self/statm")
                if (!f.canRead()) null else f.readText().trim().split(' ').getOrNull(1)?.toLongOrNull()?.times(4096L)
            }.getOrNull()
            if (android != null && android > 0L) return android
            // JVM fallback returns 0 (PolicyGuardTest forbids shell commands to keep the no shell rule).
            return 0L
        }
    }
}
```

## `app/src/main/java/com/cleanforge/core/cleaning/CleaningEngine.kt`

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.cleaning

import com.cleanforge.core.backend.Capabilities
import com.cleanforge.core.backend.FileOperationBackend
import com.cleanforge.core.backend.FsResult
import com.cleanforge.core.backend.InstallState
import com.cleanforge.core.backend.MIN_PLAUSIBLE_PACKAGES
import com.cleanforge.core.backend.PackageInventory
import com.cleanforge.core.model.CleaningCategory
import com.cleanforge.core.model.CleaningReport
import com.cleanforge.core.model.ConfirmedPlan
import com.cleanforge.core.model.ItemOutcome
import com.cleanforge.core.model.ItemStatus
import com.cleanforge.core.model.ScanItem
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.FailureKind
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.MaintenanceResult
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.OperationCapability
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.PrivilegedExecutor
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.PrivilegedOperation
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.classifyDeletion
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.observePostState
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.toMaintenanceRequest
import com.cleanforge.core.safety.SafetyValidator
import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.currentCoroutineContext
import kotlinx.coroutines.ensureActive
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flowOn

sealed interface CleaningProgress {
    data class Started(val total: Int) : CleaningProgress

    /** Emitted BEFORE an item is touched, so a stop request can say which item was in flight. */
    data class ItemStarted(val index: Int, val total: Int, val item: ScanItem) : CleaningProgress

    /** [outcome] is the finished item's result; the UI keeps them so a stopped run still has an accurate report. */
    data class Progress(
        val done: Int,
        val total: Int,
        val freedBytes: Long,
        val currentName: String,
        val outcome: ItemOutcome? = null
    ) : CleaningProgress

    data class Completed(val report: CleaningReport) : CleaningProgress
}

/**
 * Executes a [ConfirmedPlan]. Pipeline per item:
 *   REVALIDATE (policy + live capabilities + fresh evidence + fingerprint) -> DELETE -> VERIFY -> REPORT.
 * Sequential on purpose: gentle on a low-end eMMC and trivially cancellable between items.
 * Nothing in here accepts a ScanItem list directly; a human-confirmed plan is the only entry point.
 *
 * Privileged items (Android/data caches, uninstalled-app leftovers) go through [PrivilegedExecutor] as typed
 * maintenance requests; everything else runs in this process through [standardBackend]. An item that cannot be mapped
 * to a supported privileged operation is skipped with a reason, never run as some weaker operation.
 */
class CleaningEngine(
    private val safety: SafetyValidator,
    private val standardBackend: FileOperationBackend,
    private val privileged: PrivilegedExecutor,
    private val inventory: PackageInventory,
    private val capabilities: Capabilities
) {

    /**
     * What ONE run has already established, so a plan of hundreds of items does not repeat the two expensive questions
     * (the full package list, the Shizuku capability probe) for every item. A new run starts empty: nothing is reused
     * across runs. The cheap, per-package install state and the Shizuku authorization are still asked for every item.
     */
    private class RunCache {
        var knownPackages: Set<String>? = null
        val ready = HashMap<PrivilegedOperation, OperationCapability>()
    }

    fun execute(confirmed: ConfirmedPlan): Flow<CleaningProgress> = flow {
        val cache = RunCache()
        val items = confirmed.plan.items
        val outcomes = ArrayList<ItemOutcome>(items.size)
        var freed = 0L
        emit(CleaningProgress.Started(items.size))
        for ((index, item) in items.withIndex()) {
            currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()
            emit(CleaningProgress.ItemStarted(index + 1, items.size, item))
            val outcome = try {
                processItem(item, cache)
            } catch (ce: CancellationException) {
                throw ce
            } catch (t: Throwable) {
                // A failing capability/inventory call must cost ONE item, not the whole run and its report.
                failed(item, t.message ?: "Cleanup failed unexpectedly")
            }
            outcomes += outcome
            freed += outcome.bytesFreed
            emit(CleaningProgress.Progress(index + 1, items.size, freed, item.displayName, outcome))
        }
        emit(CleaningProgress.Completed(CleaningReport(outcomes)))
    }.flowOn(Dispatchers.IO)

    private suspend fun processItem(item: ScanItem, cache: RunCache): ItemOutcome {
        // ---- REVALIDATE ----
        val refusal = safety.rejectionReason(item)
        if (refusal != null) return skipped(item, "Safety check failed: $refusal")

        if (!item.requiresShizuku && !capabilities.hasAllFilesAccess()) {
            return skipped(item, "All-files access is no longer granted")
        }
        if (item.requiresShizuku && !capabilities.shizukuAuthorized()) {
            return skipped(item, "Shizuku is not available right now")
        }

        var known: Set<String> = emptySet()
        if (item.category == CleaningCategory.CORPSE_LEFTOVER || item.category == CleaningCategory.APP_CACHE) {
            val pkg = item.owningPackage ?: return skipped(item, "No package recorded for this folder")
            val snapshot = cache.knownPackages ?: inventory.knownPackageNames()
            if (snapshot == null || snapshot.size < MIN_PLAUSIBLE_PACKAGES) {
                return skipped(item, "Could not verify which apps are installed")
            }
            cache.knownPackages = snapshot
            known = snapshot
            // Two different questions: "known" includes data-kept uninstalls, "installed" does not. A failed query is
            // UNKNOWN and is never read as "not installed" (that would be the unsafe answer for a leftover).
            val state = inventory.installState(pkg)
            if (state == InstallState.UNKNOWN) return skipped(item, "Could not verify whether $pkg is installed")
            if (item.category == CleaningCategory.CORPSE_LEFTOVER) {
                val knownLower = known.any { it.equals(pkg, ignoreCase = true) }
                if (state != InstallState.NOT_KNOWN || pkg in known || knownLower) {
                    return skipped(item, "$pkg is known to Android again; its folder is no longer a leftover")
                }
            } else if (state != InstallState.INSTALLED || pkg !in known) {
                return skipped(item, "$pkg is not currently installed")
            }
        }

        return if (item.requiresShizuku) processPrivileged(item, known, cache) else processStandard(item)
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- privileged path

    private suspend fun processPrivileged(item: ScanItem, known: Set<String>, cache: RunCache): ItemOutcome {
        val expected = item.fingerprint ?: return skipped(item, "No scan snapshot for this item; scan again")
        val request = item.toMaintenanceRequest(known)
            ?: return skipped(item, "This item is not a kind of cleanup the Shizuku service supports, so it was left alone")

        val readiness = cache.ready[request.operation]
            ?: capabilities.readiness(request.operation).also { if (it.canAttempt) cache.ready[request.operation] = it }
        if (!readiness.canAttempt) return skipped(item, "Not available right now: ${readiness.reason}")

        when (val now = privileged.stat(item.path)) {
            is FsResult.Ok -> if (!now.value.sameObjectAs(expected)) {
                return skipped(item, "Changed since the scan; scan again to include it")
            }
            FsResult.NotFound -> return skipped(item, "Already gone")
            is FsResult.Unavailable -> return failed(item, "The Shizuku service could not be reached: ${now.why}")
            is FsResult.Denied -> return failed(item, "Could not examine this item: ${now.why}")
            is FsResult.Failed -> return failed(item, "Could not examine this item: ${now.why}")
        }

        val result = try {
            privileged.execute(request)
        } catch (ce: CancellationException) {
            throw ce
        } catch (t: Throwable) {
            return failed(item, t.message ?: "Cleanup failed unexpectedly")
        }
        return outcomeFrom(item, result)
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- standard (app process) path

    private suspend fun processStandard(item: ScanItem): ItemOutcome {
        if (item.category == CleaningCategory.DUPLICATE) {
            if (item.keepPath == item.path) return skipped(item, "The copy that should stay is this very file")
            val keepThen = item.keepFingerprint
            val keepNow = item.keepPath?.let { (standardBackend.lstat(it) as? FsResult.Ok)?.value }
            if (keepNow == null || keepThen == null || !keepNow.sameObjectAs(keepThen)) {
                return skipped(item, "The copy that should stay changed or disappeared")
            }
        }

        val expected = item.fingerprint ?: return skipped(item, "No scan snapshot for this item; scan again")
        when (val now = standardBackend.lstat(item.path)) {
            is FsResult.Ok -> if (!now.value.sameObjectAs(expected)) {
                return skipped(item, "Changed since the scan; scan again to include it")
            }
            FsResult.NotFound -> return skipped(item, "Already gone")
            is FsResult.Unavailable -> return failed(item, "Could not examine this item: ${now.why}")
            is FsResult.Denied -> return failed(item, "Could not examine this item: ${now.why}")
            is FsResult.Failed -> return failed(item, "Could not examine this item: ${now.why}")
        }

        // ---- DELETE ----
        val result = try {
            standardBackend.delete(item.path, item.deleteMode, expected)
        } catch (ce: CancellationException) {
            throw ce
        } catch (t: Throwable) {
            return failed(item, t.message ?: "Delete failed unexpectedly")
        }

        // ---- VERIFY ----
        val post = observePostState(item.path, item.deleteMode, { standardBackend.lstat(it) }, { standardBackend.list(it) })
        return outcomeFrom(item, classifyDeletion(item.deleteMode, result, post))
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- reporting

    /** The only place a [MaintenanceResult] becomes a user-visible status. */
    private fun outcomeFrom(item: ScanItem, r: MaintenanceResult): ItemOutcome = when (r) {
        is MaintenanceResult.Success -> ItemOutcome(item, ItemStatus.DELETED, r.message, r.bytesFreed)
        is MaintenanceResult.Partial -> ItemOutcome(item, ItemStatus.PARTIAL, r.message, r.bytesFreed)
        is MaintenanceResult.Unverified -> ItemOutcome(item, ItemStatus.UNVERIFIED, r.message, r.bytesFreed)
        is MaintenanceResult.Unsupported -> skipped(item, "Not available right now: ${r.message}")
        is MaintenanceResult.Failure -> when (r.kind) {
            FailureKind.PRECONDITION_CHANGED, FailureKind.REFUSED -> skipped(item, r.message)
            FailureKind.UNAVAILABLE, FailureKind.LIMIT, FailureKind.CANCELLED, FailureKind.IO_ERROR ->
                ItemOutcome(item, ItemStatus.FAILED, r.message, r.bytesFreed)
        }
    }

    private fun skipped(item: ScanItem, why: String) = ItemOutcome(item, ItemStatus.SKIPPED, why)
    private fun failed(item: ScanItem, why: String) = ItemOutcome(item, ItemStatus.FAILED, why)
}
```

## `app/src/main/java/com/cleanforge/core/cleaning/PermissionAnnotator.kt`

```kotlin
package com.cleanforge.core.cleaning

import com.cleanforge.core.backend.Capabilities
import com.cleanforge.core.model.CleaningCategory
import com.cleanforge.core.model.CleaningPlan
import com.cleanforge.core.model.PermissionNeed
import com.cleanforge.core.model.PermissionNote
import com.cleanforge.core.privileged.PrivilegedOperation
import javax.inject.Inject
import javax.inject.Singleton

@Singleton
class PermissionAnnotator @Inject constructor(private val capabilities: Capabilities) {

    suspend fun annotate(plan: CleaningPlan): CleaningPlan {
        val allFiles = capabilities.hasAllFilesAccess()
        val shizuku = capabilities.shizukuAuthorized()
        val notes = LinkedHashMap<String, PermissionNote>(plan.items.size)
        var blocking = false
        for (item in plan.items) {
            val note = if (item.requiresShizuku) {
                val op = when (item.category) {
                    CleaningCategory.CORPSE_LEFTOVER -> PrivilegedOperation.REMOVE_UNINSTALLED_APP_DATA
                    else -> PrivilegedOperation.CLEAR_EXTERNAL_APP_CACHE
                }
                if (!shizuku) {
                    PermissionNote(
                        need = PermissionNeed.SHIZUKU_OPERATION,
                        required = true,
                        available = false,
                        detail = "Shizuku is not available right now; this item will be skipped."
                    )
                } else {
                    val cap = capabilities.readiness(op)
                    PermissionNote(
                        need = PermissionNeed.SHIZUKU_OPERATION,
                        required = true,
                        available = cap.canAttempt,
                        detail = if (cap.canAttempt) "Shizuku is ready for ${op.title}."
                        else "Shizuku: ${cap.status} — ${cap.reason}. This item will be skipped."
                    )
                }
            } else if (!allFiles) {
                PermissionNote(
                    need = PermissionNeed.ALL_FILES,
                    required = true,
                    available = false,
                    detail = "All-files access is missing; this item will be skipped."
                )
            } else {
                PermissionNote(
                    need = PermissionNeed.ALL_FILES,
                    required = true,
                    available = true,
                    detail = "All-files access is granted."
                )
            }
            notes[item.path] = note
            if (note.blocking) blocking = true
        }
        return plan.copy(permissionNotes = notes, hasBlockingPermissions = blocking)
    }
}
```
